outcome.technical:
tools/affected.py:
(1) The reach graph now walks `.claude/hooks/` (REPO_HOOKS, REACH_DIRS:244). Hooks count as development code (_is_dev:279) and as runners (_is_runner:598), so a plugin change selects `python3 .claude/hooks/<hook>.py --selftest`. That alone turned a18n/a18o/a18p green: guard-release imports _manifest_io/_manifest_vocab/_worktrees off a sys.path entry it assembles itself, and arm-release-bypass loads guard-release by a joined path.
(2) A path assembled from literal pieces is read as the literal it spells (_assembled:321). That covers os.path.join/posixpath.join (leading non-literal roots dropped), `+`, and module-level constants holding either, resolved in order so a constant built from an earlier one resolves (_py_constants:347, which now returns every assembled module string). _scan marks join arguments and `+` operands as PIECES, so a piece is never read as a whole path from the repo root (_note_path:368). One side effect: a shipped module resolving `find_script(CONST)` through an assembled constant now names its target instead of widening to every script (a20e).
(3) For item 2, the edge the graph did not read is a DOCUMENT. tests/test_derive_phase_gate.py reads `os.path.join(_output.REPO_ROOT, 'CONTRIBUTING.md')` and runs the listing commands recorded there, which name tools/affected.py. Same rule as (1): the assembled `.md` path is recorded (scan['docs']), and for development code the `python3 <path>.py` commands that document records become run edges (_doc_command_stems:382, _file_edges:523, reach_graph:578). The lookup is exact-case so the selection does not differ on case-insensitive filesystems.
Cases: rows a18n,a18o,a18p (d36d84e8, 0b856d0c, 862b4941) and a18q (a1891691) in MEASURED_MISSES; a20 (direct join, assembled name), a20b (constant via `+` where no call is open), a20c (constant built from earlier constants), a20d (other direction: an unused constant names nothing), a20e (shipped hook via constant: precise, not unknown), a20f (document via join and via bare `+`; a join piece not read alone), a20g (document edge; shipped code naming a document reaches nothing; case-folded name rejected). Each of a20, a20b and a20c checks a suite, a tool and a hook. affected.py --selftest: 52/52.
Widening, measured once (<scratchpad>/p1434/widen.py, HEAD selector vs this one, every tracked .py outside .claude/hooks): over 352 paths the total selection mass goes from 27029 to 27763 (+2.7%), 151 paths change, 0 narrow. The extra mass comes from documents several suites read (README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, CLAUDE.md, PLUGIN-BUILD-GUIDE.md) whose commands become edges, which over-approximates in the allowed direction.

tools/measure-affected-miss.py:
(3) Item 3: under a mutation, _sweep:524 starts the runner through SHADOW_LAUNCHER:160 (write_shadow:501). The launcher's import hook compiles the HELD unmutated bytes of every mutated file, under the tree's own path, so __file__-derived paths stay the tree's and no mutated .pyc is trusted. It also runs the unmutated runner bytes as __main__. Every suite the runner starts is a fresh interpreter on the mutated tree, the runner's own suite included. Scratch goes outside the tree and is removed in finally. Sweeps after restore run as before. Case m21: a fixture commit changing the runner and the lint it imports is measured; the lint's suite and the runner's own suite are the misses; no scratch is left. Real-runner check (<scratchpad>/p1434/real_runner.py, scratch worktree at HEAD, raise planted in tools/sweep-selftests.py and tools/lints/_output_lints.py, paths tools/sweep-selftests.py tools/where.py tests/test__runner_output.py): plain sweep complete=False ('...sweep-selftests.py, line 2 ... raise'); shadowed complete=True, red=['tools/sweep-selftests.py']; restored tree red=[]; no scratch left.
(4) Item 4: the Windows miss on 94a097d7 is a PLATFORM-ONLY red, not a selection miss. Evidence: CI run 40511735770 (ci/P142, sha 94a097d7). `gh run view --log-failed` names one failing suite, tests/_harness.py, and only in 'selftests (windows, cp1252 1)' and 'selftests (windows, plain 1)'. `gh run view --json jobs` shows 'selftests (linux, plain 1)' and every other linux selftests job concluded success. The commit itself changed only tools/prove-gates.py, and the CRLF fault lived in tests/_harness.py. The measurement now reports such reds apart: parse_ci_log_jobs:319, job_conclusions:786 and platform_only:339. A suite counts as platform-only only when every job naming it ran on a non-posix runner, at least one posix twin of those jobs concluded success, and no twin concluded otherwise; a twin-less leg (cp1252) neither proves nor refutes. render prints 'platform-only  CI run ...' lines and ', N platform-only red(s) set apart' (render:954). Applied to the real run, the reading gives platform_only == ['tests/_harness.py']. Case m22 covers runs 6-9 (platform-only; cancelled twin; a posix job also named it; a twin-less leg only). measure-affected-miss.py --selftest: 27/27.
